title: Metric reasoning and trace tags - lab notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes and lightweight decision log for metric definitions, trace tag conventions, and a compact dashboard layout we can prototype this sprint. Aim: reduce ambiguity in SLI rollups, simplify operator drilldowns, and cap query cost while keeping enough context for root cause.

Context and constraints:
- Multi-tenant inference runtime: per-tenant cost attribution, per-model routing, fallback variants, and KV cache behavior matter for latency and cost signals.
- Cost sensitivity: dashboards must avoid high-cardinality joins by default; sampled traces provide fine-grain context.
- Operator-first: oncall must be able to go from alert -> 3 panels -> trace within 90s.

High-level goals (short):
- Make a canonical set of runtime metrics that map directly to SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency, cold-starts, kvcache warmth, token rate, error-rate).
- Define trace tags and span anchors needed for investigations (tenant_id, route, model_version, kv_warmth_hint).
- Propose a compact dashboard layout to cover surface area for rollouts and incident TTR.

Metric definitions (candidate canonical names and notes):
1) inference.latency_ms{percentile, route, model} - latency from request-received to last-token-emitted. Use histogram -> percentiles. Exclude client disconnects.
   - Unit: ms
   - Alert anchor: p99 > 1200ms for 5m AND traffic > 50 req/min
   - Why: single-number SLO mapping and lat attribution.

2) inference.first_token_ms{route, model} - time to first token (client-perceived). Helps detect cold-path kernel or model load stalls.
   - Unit: ms
   - Investigator tip: large delta between first_token and tail indicates KV/decoder backpressure.

3) inference.kvcache.hit_rate{model, tenant, route} - fraction of requests served with satisfied prefix/KV hits.
   - Unit: ratio (0-1) sampled as 1s rolling window
   - Implementation note: if full-resolution tenant dimension is high-card, default to tenant_tier (free/paid/enterprise) and a sampled tenant list for deep-dive.

4) inference.tokens_per_second{model, worker_pool} - steady-state throughput per worker.
   - Unit: tokens/s
   - Use: capacity projections and autoscaler tuning.

5) inference.error_rate{class, route} - 4xx/5xx split and model-failures (OOM, kernel-fail).
   - Unit: errors / request
   - Alert: 5xx > 1% sustained for 5m AND absolute errors > 20/min

6) routing.fallback_rate{route, region} - fraction of requests that fell back to variant or lower-tier model.
   - Why: operationally useful to separate capacity-induced fallbacks vs policy rollouts.

7) model.load_time_ms{model_version, host} - time taken to instantiate model binary on worker. Flag spikes for on-demand scale-ups.

8) request.size_tokens{percentile, route} - request token counts; used to normalize latency by input length.

Trace tag & span conventions (proposal):
- Trace root: trace.id -> span[0] annotated with request_id, tenant_id (hashed), route, route_config_id, model_version, region, tracing_level.
- Span anchors:
  - span.request-receive: timestamp when front-end accepted request (tags: frontend_host, client_sdk)
  - span.routing-decision: which pool and fallback chosen (tags: decision, reason_code)
  - span.model-invoke: per-model span containing kvcache_hit bool, kv_prefetch_duration_ms, decode_duration_ms, tokens_emitted
  - span.model-load (if on-demand): includes artifact_size_bytes, quantization_profile
  - span.grpc-or-io: network and serialization overheads between services
- Tag naming: use dot-separated lower_snake (e.g., tenant_id_hash, kv_hit, model_variant). Keep tag names small to reduce indexing cost.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling with severity weights - sample all traces where p99_latency > threshold or where routing.fallback=true or error_rate>0.5% for that minute. Otherwise 1% reservoir by default.

Dashboard sketch (compact, 6-panel strip):
Left column (fast triage):
- Panel A: SLO overview (p50/p95/p99, error rate) with traffic sparkline. Controls: time window, tenant_tier filter.
- Panel B: Alerting states & recent incidents (linked to timeline + short blame tags).

Center column (latency attribution):
- Panel C: Latency decomposition waterfall (first_token, kv_prefetch, decode, tail) stacked percentiles by route. Dropdown: model_version.
- Panel D: KV cache warmth heatmap (model x hour) and top 10 tenants by cold rate.

Right column (operational knobs):
- Panel E: Routing/fallbacks (fallback_rate over time by region + recent fallback reasons).
- Panel F: Top traces quicklist (sampled traces for last 15m flagged by p99 or error), with one-click open in trace viewer.

Panel UX notes:
- Default views should be low-cardinality; expanders allow tenant-level and worker-level detail.
- Add query budget indicator at top-right: "estimated cost: X credits" for the selected time range.
- Widgets must have deep-links to pre-baked trace filter queries.

Investigation recipes (operator shortcuts):
1) Slow p99 on a route: check panel C waterfall -> if kv_prefetch spike, look at kvcache hit_rate and model.load_time; open trace where kv_hit=false.
2) Surprising fallback spike: open Panel E, filter by reason_code, compare model.load_time and worker_pool_util. If both normal, escalate to autoscaler.
3) Token amplification (cost spike): check tokens_per_request distribution and embeddings/regen loops.

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide in followup:
- tenant dimension cardinality: keep tenant_id hashed in metrics, and allow sampled tenant rollups in a separate low-card channel? (pros: privacy + costs; cons: slower deep-dive).
- Should we expose kv_warmth_hint as a metric or only via traces? Metric helps alerting but increases cardinality.
- Sampling policy thresholds: where to place p99 threshold for always-sample traces per route? Need a small pilot with 5 routes.

Short experiment plan for next sprint (owner tags):
- [Priya] Implement inference.kvcache.hit_rate aggregation by tenant_tier and model; add one sampled tenant list (5 tenants) for deep-dive - finish by 2026-02-12.
- [Ethan] Add trace tag 'kv_hit' and ensure model-invoke span emits kv_prefetch_duration_ms - finish by 2026-02-10.
- [Zoe] Prototype dashboard strip in dev Grafana with query-cost banner; demo 2026-02-16.

Action items (immediate):
- Approve metric names (this doc) and publish short naming guide (1-pager) - deadline 2026-02-07.
- Create Jira tickets for sampling pilot and tenant sampling infra.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep metric names stable: changing names breaks SLO alarms; prefer labels over new metrics where possible.
- For high-card tenants, use cardinality buckets (top-20, sampled, rest) and a cheap counter metric for bottom group.

References and links:
- Confluence draft: OBS-1881 metric taxonomy (linked above)
- Prior dashboard wireframes: slack thread #obs-dashboard-ux (see pinned messages)

End of lab notes.

Unresolved: confirm biz-visibility needs for per-tenant p95 SLA for enterprise customers (Anna to confirm).

-- Priya
